title: ‘A Prophet’: The Zeal of Bernie Sanders Supporters

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》每日简报栏目 DealBook 的商业与政策记者。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的一些领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经滤镜的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用来观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Of a man by the name of Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 一个名叫伯尼·桑德斯的人。

sentences.en: And to question and assert and recognize my inherent value as a human being that deserves health care, housing, education, and a living wage.
sentences.zh: 并且去质疑、主张并认可我作为一个人应有的内在价值，我理应获得医疗保健、住房、教育和体面的生活工资。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: They're very unhappy that Bernie is back.
sentences.zh: 他们对伯尼的回归感到非常不满。

sentences.en: Bernie Sanders drew the largest crowd of his campaign yet at a rally in New York City last weekend, at a moment when his candidacy may be at its most vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 上周末，在纽约市的一场集会上，伯尼·桑德斯吸引了他竞选以来最大规模的人群，而此时他的候选人资格可能正处于最脆弱的时刻。

sentences.en: The only heart attack we should be talking about is the one Wall Street is going to have.
sentences.zh: 我们唯一应该谈论的心脏病发作，应该是华尔街将要经历的那一次。

sentences.en: Those crowds are raising a fraught question for the leaders of the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 这些民众给民主党领导层提出了一个棘手的问题。

sentences.en: Is the loyalty of Sanders supporters to the party or just to him?
sentences.zh: 桑德斯支持者的忠诚度是对党的，还是仅仅对他个人？

sentences.en: I don't know why you would take the courage, you know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你为什么要拿出勇气，你知道的。

sentences.en: It's Friday, October 25th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月25日，星期五。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm a producer at the New York Times a daily.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是《纽约时报》《每日新闻》的一名制作人。

sentences.en: Can I ask you guys a few questions?
sentences.zh: 我能问你们几个问题吗？

sentences.en: Alex Burns, we're going to do something a little bit different here.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯·伯恩斯，我们在这里要做点稍微不一样的事情。

sentences.en: My colleague, Daily producer Jessica Chung, went to this Bernie Sanders rally over the weekend in Queens, New York.
sentences.zh: 我的同事、《每日新闻》制作人杰西卡·钟上周末去了纽约皇后区这场伯尼·桑德斯的集会。

sentences.en: And she recorded everything that she heard.
sentences.zh: 她录下了她听到的一切。

sentences.en: What brought you out here today?
sentences.zh: 是什么把你吸引到这里来的？

sentences.en: We love Bernie.
sentences.zh: 我们爱伯尼。

sentences.en: I'm a huge Bernie fan.
sentences.zh: 我是伯尼的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: I've always supported Bernie even before I could vote.
sentences.zh: 我一直支持伯尼，甚至在我有投票权之前就开始了。

sentences.en: And it felt to her and it felt to us that she had really picked the right Bernie Sanders rally to attend if you're going to attend just one.
sentences.zh: 对她来说，对我们来说，如果我们只打算参加一场伯尼·桑德斯的集会，她确实选对了去处。

sentences.en: She really did.
sentences.zh: 她真的选对了。

sentences.en: This came at a huge moment for the Sanders campaign.
sentences.zh: 这对桑德斯的竞选活动来说是一个关键时刻。

sentences.en: It was a huge test for the Sanders campaign.
sentences.zh: 这是对桑德斯竞选团队的一场巨大考验。

sentences.en: We got a permit for 20,000 people and we have to close the doors.
sentences.zh: 我们申请了容纳两万人的许可证，现在我们不得不关门谢客了。

sentences.en: It has been a tough stretch for Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 对伯尼·桑德斯来说，这是一段艰难的时期。

sentences.en: He had a heart attack.
sentences.zh: 他心脏病发作了。

sentences.en: He was off the trail for a couple weeks ahead of this rally with the exception of the debate in Ohio.
sentences.zh: 除了在俄亥俄州的辩论外，在这次集会之前，他有几周时间离开竞选活动。

sentences.en: Before the heart attack, the race was showing signs of becoming really a two-candidate contest between Elizabeth Warren and Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 心脏病发作前，这场竞选已经显示出真正变成伊丽莎白·沃伦和乔·拜登两人之争的迹象。

sentences.en: And Sanders was really struggling to show that he still had a path to win this thing, not just to be relevant, but to win this thing.
sentences.zh: 桑德斯当时在艰难地证明他仍然有赢得这场竞选的途径，而不仅仅是保持存在感，而是要赢得这场竞选。

sentences.en: And so these forces really converge in Queens.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些力量在皇后区汇聚到了一起。

sentences.en: I want you all to take a look around and find someone you don't know.
sentences.zh: 我希望你们所有人环顾四周，找一个你们不认识的人。

sentences.en: Maybe somebody who doesn't look kind of like you.
sentences.zh: 也许是一个长得跟你不太一样的人。

sentences.en: Maybe somebody who might be of a different religion than you.
sentences.zh: 也许是一个信仰不同宗教的人。

sentences.en: Maybe they come from a different country.
sentences.zh: 也许他们来自不同的国家。

sentences.en: My question now to you is, are you willing to fight for that person who you don't even know as much as you're willing to fight for yourself?
sentences.zh: 我现在给你们的问题是：你们是否愿意为了那个甚至不认识的人去抗争，就像你们愿意为自己抗争那样？

sentences.en: And he delivers a speech that is, in most respects, not thematically groundbreaking.
sentences.zh: 他发表了一场在大多数方面主题上并没有突破性的演讲。

sentences.en: It's about the big ideas of his campaign.
sentences.zh: 它关乎他竞选的核心理念。

sentences.en: Today in America, half of our population is living paycheck to paycheck, struggling to pay their rents, their mortgages, their light bill, or fix their car.
sentences.zh: 今天的美国，我们有一半的人口过着靠薪水度日的生活，艰难地支付房租、按揭贷款、电费，或者修车费用。

sentences.en: Economic inequality, Medicare for all corruption in Washington and on Wall Street.
sentences.zh: 经济不平等、全民医保、华盛顿和华尔街的腐败。

sentences.en: But he rolls out one of the biggest endorsements a progressive candidate can get, Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez,
sentences.zh: 但他推出了进步派候选人能获得的最高规格背书之一，即众议员亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯，

sentences.en: and delivers his message with a force that is intended to really convey the idea that Bernie is back.
sentences.zh: 并以一种旨在强烈传达“伯尼回来了”这一信息的力度发表了他的演讲。

sentences.en: In fact, I think he says...
sentences.zh: 事实上，我想他是这么说的……

sentences.en: To put it bluntly, I am back.
sentences.zh: 直截了当地说，我回来了。

sentences.en: I'm back.
sentences.zh: 我回来了。

sentences.en: Which is an acknowledgment, of course, that he needs a comeback.
sentences.zh: 当然，这承认了他需要一场东山再起。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think he has really resisted the idea that he has fallen behind in this race, but it's manifestly clear that he has.
sentences.zh: 我认为他一直在极力抗拒自己在这次竞选中落后的说法，但很明显他确实落后了。

sentences.en: And from his body language, from his rhetoric, from the way his campaign is now approaching the early states and big events like this one,
sentences.zh: 从他的肢体语言、他的言辞，以及他的竞选团队现在对待早期州和类似这样的大型活动的方式来看，

sentences.en: it's clear that they know he does need a comeback.
sentences.zh: 很明显他们知道他的确需要一场东山再起。

sentences.en: I am more than ready to assume the office of President of the United States.
sentences.zh: 我已经做好了充分准备来担任美利坚合众国总统。

sentences.en: And because his campaign is at this pivotal moment, we wanted to better understand his supporters and the nature of his support.
sentences.zh: 正因为他的竞选正处于这个关键时刻，我们想要更好地了解他的支持者以及他支持者的本质。

sentences.en: What somebody who shows up at a Bernie Sanders rally thinks about Sanders, how they talk about him, and what that means for the Democratic primary.
sentences.zh: 一个出现在伯尼·桑德斯集会上的如何看待桑德斯，他们如何谈论他，以及这对民主党初选意味着什么。

sentences.en: So that's what Jessica ended up asking voters about.
sentences.zh: 这就是杰西卡最终向选民们询问的问题。

sentences.en: And so I want to play that for you.
sentences.zh: 所以我想把这些放给你们听。

sentences.en: What about him excites you?
sentences.zh: 他身上什么地方让你兴奋？

sentences.en: Bernie is the true progressive, the only true progressive running in the race.
sentences.zh: 伯尼是真正的进步派，是竞选中唯一的真正进步派。

sentences.en: Bernie doesn't say, leave it to me.
sentences.zh: 伯尼不说“交给我吧”。

sentences.en: Bernie says, come with me.
sentences.zh: 伯尼说“跟我来”。

sentences.en: We must join forces to create the fundamental changes required in this society.
sentences.zh: 我们必须联合起来，创造这个社会所需的根本变革。

sentences.en: If you look at Bernie's record, Bernie's been just saying the same things since pretty much like the 60s or whenever he came into public office.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看伯尼的记录，伯尼说的基本上从60年代或者他进入公职以来就一直没变过。

sentences.en: The 80s.
sentences.zh: 80年代。

sentences.en: Yeah, sorry.
sentences.zh: 对，抱歉。

sentences.en: The 80s.
sentences.zh: 80年代。

sentences.en: And so I think now there's a lot of people that are, like, jumping onto the bandwagon.
sentences.zh: 所以我想现在有很多人都在盲目跟风。

sentences.en: And so I really just think it's the strength of Bernie Sanders and his platform.
sentences.zh: 因此我真的认为这正是伯尼·桑德斯及其政纲的力量所在。

sentences.en: He's a prophet.
sentences.zh: 他是先知。

sentences.en: He knows the way forward.
sentences.zh: 他知道前进的道路。

sentences.en: What you hear there is just the extraordinary stature that Sanders commands on the left.
sentences.zh: 你在那里听到的是桑德斯在左翼拥有的非凡地位。

sentences.en: The real fruits of that campaign that he ran in 2015 and 2016 when he got out there into an ideological space that other Democrats were just not comfortable entering and ran an insurgent campaign against the party establishment in a way that most Democrats had really never seen before.
sentences.zh: 这是他在2015年和2016年参加的那场竞选的真正成果，当时他进入了一个其他民主党人根本不敢涉足的思想领域，并以一种大多数民主党人从未见过的方式，向党内建制派发起了起义式的竞选。

sentences.en: So, you know, I think you rarely hear candidates referred to as prophets.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我认为你很少听到候选人被称为先知。

sentences.en: But even stopping short of that sort of quasi-religious language,
sentences.zh: 但即使抛开这种准宗教色彩的语言不谈，

sentences.en: the depth of commitment to Bernie Sanders among his supporters probably exceeds the bond that any other candidate in the race has with their voters.
sentences.zh: 支持者对伯尼·桑德斯的忠诚度，可能超过了竞选中任何其他候选人与选民之间的纽带。

sentences.en: Greater even than Trump?
sentences.zh: 甚至比特朗普还要深厚？

sentences.en: Or you mean greater even than anyone on the Democratic field?
sentences.zh: 还是说你指的是比民主党阵营里的任何人都要深厚？

sentences.en: On the Democratic side, I should say.
sentences.zh: 我是说在民主党这一边。

sentences.en: It is probably closer to Trump than to any of the other Democrats.
sentences.zh: 这可能更接近特朗普，而不是其他任何民主党人。

sentences.en: That's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: But, I mean, at the end of the day, a vote is a vote no matter how enthusiastically someone casts it, right?
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，归根结底，无论投票的人表现得多么热情，一票就是一票，对吧？

sentences.en: So I wonder what this kind of next-level devotion means for his candidacy.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇这种更高层级的忠诚对他的候选人资格意味着什么。

sentences.en: Well, it has meant that even in what was a very lean summer for him, just a challenging political time where he was being eclipsed by another candidate on the left,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这意味着即使在他度过了一个非常惨淡的夏天——那是一段充满挑战的政治时期，他被左翼的另一位候选人伊丽莎白·沃伦所黯然失色，

sentences.en: Elizabeth Warren, he has never really been at risk of being irrelevant in this race,
sentences.zh: 他在这场竞选中从未真正面临被边缘化的风险，

sentences.en: of being truly sidelined because right now it looks like anywhere between 10 and 17 or 18 percent of the Democratic Party is very, very tightly bonded to Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 从未真正出局，因为现在看起来，民主党内有10%到17%或18%的人与伯尼·桑德斯有着非常非常紧密的联系。

sentences.en: One out of five Democrats.
sentences.zh: 五分之一的民主党人。

sentences.en: One out of five on a good day, closer to one out of 10 on a bad day.
sentences.zh: 状态好时五分之一，状态差时接近十分之一。

sentences.en: But still, on his worst day, he's got more support in the party than every other candidate in the race except for Joe Biden and Elizabeth Warren.
sentences.zh: 但即便在他最糟糕的时候，他在党内的支持率也超过了竞选中除了乔·拜登和伊丽莎白·沃伦之外的所有其他候选人。

sentences.en: That's a pretty good place to be.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当不错的位置。

sentences.en: And his support is different from any other candidate in the race.
sentences.zh: 而且他的支持率与竞选中的任何其他候选人都不同。

sentences.en: It is particularly strong among young people.
sentences.zh: 他在年轻人中尤为强劲。

sentences.en: There's the irony of the Bernie Sanders campaign, the guy who would be the oldest president ever, the oldest candidate in this race.
sentences.zh: 这就是伯尼·桑德斯竞选的讽刺之处，这个本可能成为史上最年长的总统、这场竞选中最年长的候选人，

sentences.en: His strongest age group is the youngest age group in the Democratic electorate.
sentences.zh: 他最强的年龄段却是民主党选民中最年轻的年龄段。

sentences.en: What it has also meant is that he has this incredible flow of cash into his campaign, almost irrespective of whatever else is happening in this race.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着他的竞选资金源源不断，几乎不受这场竞选中其他任何事情的影响。

sentences.en: He has a small donor online fundraising machine that has collected tens of millions of dollars for him every quarter that he has been in this race.
sentences.zh: 他拥有一个小型捐赠者在线筹款机器，在他参加竞选的每个季度都为他筹集了数千万美元。

sentences.en: And in the most recent quarter, he was the number one fundraiser in the Democratic field.
sentences.zh: 在最近的一个季度里，他是民主党阵营中筹款最多的人。

sentences.en: That's an extraordinary thing to say about a candidate who isn't running a super PAC, isn't holding conventional big donor events, and is running on democratic socialism,
sentences.zh: 对于一个没有运行超级政治行动委员会、不举办传统的大额捐赠活动、并且主打民主社会主义的候选人来说，能说出这样的话真是非同寻常，

sentences.en: that he's the best-funded candidate in the race.
sentences.zh: 他是竞选活动中资金最充足的候选人。

sentences.en: So his fundraising is outpacing his polling, which, correct me if I'm wrong, is quite unusual in politics.
sentences.zh: 所以他的筹款超过了他的民调支持率，如果我没记错的话，这在政治上是相当罕见的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And you basically only see it when you have these candidates who have a limited but unbelievably passionate base of support.
sentences.zh: 基本上，只有当你有这些拥有有限但极其热情的支持者基础的候选人时，你才会看到这种现象。

sentences.en: You know, just one analog for this might be the Ron Paul campaign in 2012, where he was a more marginal candidate in the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这的一个类比可能是2012年的罗恩·保罗竞选，当时他在共和党内是一个较为边缘的候选人。

sentences.en: There was never a realistic chance he was going to be the nominee.
sentences.zh: 他从未有现实的机会成为总统候选人。

sentences.en: But his support was so intense that his online fundraising just sustained him in a way that other candidates couldn't dream up.
sentences.zh: 但他的支持如此强烈，以至于他的在线筹款以其他候选人无法想象的方式维持了他。

sentences.en: Bernie Sanders has a broader appeal than that, and his fundraising is much more robuSt.
sentences.zh: 伯尼·桑德斯的吸引力比那更广，他的筹款也强劲得多。

sentences.en: So it feels like Bernie Sanders is kind of a test case for why genuine enthusiasm matters so much in politics.
sentences.zh: 所以感觉伯尼·桑德斯就像是一个测试案例，证明了为什么真正的热情在政治中如此重要。

sentences.en: His supporters are willing to do things for him that other candidate supporters may not be, right?
sentences.zh: 他的支持者愿意为他做一些其他候选人支持者可能不会做的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: That he is going to have an easier time staying financially competitive, mobilizing volunteers, and especially in some of these early voting, cold-weather states in February,
sentences.zh: 那就是他在保持财务竞争力、动员志愿者方面会更加容易，特别是在2月份的这些早期投票、天气寒冷的州，

sentences.en: getting them to actually show up and caucus in Iowa in a blizzard if necessary.
sentences.zh: 如有必要，让他们在暴风雪中真正出现并在爱荷华州参加党团会议。

sentences.en: They'll do it.
sentences.zh: 他们会做到的。

sentences.en: They'll do it.
sentences.zh: 他们会做到的。

sentences.en: So the next thing that Jess asked voters about at this Sanders rally was this heart attack that Sanders had a couple weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 所以，杰丝在桑德斯的集会上问选民的下一个问题是关于桑德斯几周前经历的那次心脏病发作。

sentences.en: This is his first rally since he just came back from a heart attack.
sentences.zh: 这是他自心脏病发作康复归来以来的第一场集会。

sentences.en: I wonder if you think that that makes him less electable in any way.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是否认为这在任何程度上降低了他的当选可能性。

sentences.en: I don't think age matters.
sentences.zh: 我不认为年龄重要。

sentences.en: I think that's a stupid, like, I don't know why people care about that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很愚蠢，比如，我不知道为什么人们要在乎这个。

sentences.en: No, because he came back stronger, and it was a routine procedure that many people go through.
sentences.zh: 不，因为他以更强的姿态回归了，这是一个许多人都会经历的常规手术。

sentences.en: I know a lot of people that have had stents put in and then felt better afterwards than before, and I think he looked great, so I'm going to stick with him.
sentences.zh: 我认识很多人，他们装了支架后感觉比以前更好了，而且我觉得他看起来状态很好，所以我打算支持他。

sentences.en: The curious thing is that Bernie, having undergone this procedure, may feel like 110% better than he did before.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，伯尼在接受了这个手术后，可能会感觉比以前好上110%。

sentences.en: Just the amount of literal blood flowing to his heart may give him a level of energy and stamina that he didn't feel before he underwent the procedure.
sentences.zh: 流向他心脏的字面血液量可能会赋予他一种在接受手术之前所没有的精力和体力水平。

sentences.en: I don't think that our current president has the best help, so why are we worried so much about a heart attack that wasn't, you know, a big deal?
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们现任总统有最好的健康状况，所以我们为什么如此担心一次并不是什么大不了的心脏病发作呢？

sentences.en: He went right back into it afterwards.
sentences.zh: 他事后立刻就投入进去了。

sentences.en: Both George Bush and Clinton had the same operation done in their 60s, so he's also pushing it, you know.
sentences.zh: 乔治·布什和克林顿都在60多岁的时候做过同样的手术，所以他也还在坚持，你知道的。

sentences.en: He is, but I mean, it doesn't, I don't, I'm not thinking about age, I'm thinking about.
sentences.zh: 他是，但我的意思是，这并没有，我不是在想年龄，我是在想……

sentences.en: There's a pretty heavy bias against Bernie Sanders because he's a fairly unique candidate.
sentences.zh: 对伯尼·桑德斯存在相当严重的偏见，因为他是一个相当独特的候选人。

sentences.en: Like, Joe Biden's eye exploded while we were all watching a debate, and they didn't single him out with a question like, hey, Joe, like, why'd your eye explode?
sentences.zh: 就像，乔·拜登的眼睛在我们都在观看辩论的时候爆裂了，而他们并没有用一个单独的问题针对他，比如，嘿，乔，你的眼睛为什么爆裂了？

sentences.en: Like, is it going to happen again?
sentences.zh: 就像，它还会再次发生吗？

sentences.en: Did I miss something?
sentences.zh: 我是不是漏掉了什么？

sentences.en: Did Joe Biden's eye suffer some kind of explosion?
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登的眼睛经历某种爆炸了吗？

sentences.en: There was a CNN town hall where he had some kind of burst capillary in his eye or something like that.
sentences.zh: 在一次美国有线电视新闻网的市民大会上，他的眼睛里某种毛细血管破裂了之类的。

sentences.en: It was unsightly, but not medically serious.
sentences.zh: 这很难看，但在医学上并不严重。

sentences.en: So, in summary, it feels like Sanders supporters in this crowd, they are not concerned about this heart attack, and I wonder what you think of the way it was discussed.
sentences.zh: 所以，总而言之，感觉这个人群中的桑德斯支持者并不担心这次心脏病发作，我想知道你对讨论它的方式有何看法。

sentences.en: I think right after the heart attack happened, there was this moment of questioning, would Sanders persist in this race?
sentences.zh: 我认为在心脏病发作发生后不久，曾有过这样一个质疑的时刻：桑德斯还会坚持参加这场竞选吗？

sentences.en: Would his health become the defining issue of his candidacy?
sentences.zh: 他的健康会成为他竞选的决定性问题吗？

sentences.en: And at least for his supporters, the answer to all those things is no.
sentences.zh: 至少对于他的支持者来说，所有这些问题的答案都是“不”。

sentences.en: They are willing to give him the benefit of the doubt on so much, and his physical health is not an exception to that.
sentences.zh: 他们在很多事情上都愿意给他受益疑归被告的宽容，而他的身体健康也不例外。

sentences.en: I think that you hear people giving rationalizations.
sentences.zh: 我想你会听到人们在给出合理的解释。

sentences.en: It's true that Bill Clinton had a similar operation.
sentences.zh: 比尔·克林顿做过类似的手术是事实。

sentences.en: It was after he was the president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 那是在他担任美国总统之后。

sentences.en: The reality is a candidate having a heart attack is a really big deal, and historically, by any standard of political coverage,
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，候选人突发心脏病是一件非常严重的事情，从历史上看，按照任何政治报道的标准，

sentences.en: it is more than inbounds as a subject for scrutiny and for voters to consider.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一个属于受审视范畴并且供选民考量的话题。

sentences.en: We've never had a president turn 80 in office before.
sentences.zh: 我们以前从未有过总统在任期内年满80岁。

sentences.en: We have two candidates in this race.
sentences.zh: 这场角逐中有两名候选人。

sentences.en: Two of the top three candidates into this race would turn 80 in their first term as president if they were elected.
sentences.zh: 如果当选，这场角逐中排名前三的候选人里有两位在他们第一任总统任期内就会年满80岁。

sentences.en: People remember, I think, pretty well Hillary Clinton fainting at the 9-11 memorial in the middle of the general election in 2016.
sentences.zh: 我想大家对2016年大选中期希拉里·克林顿在9·11纪念活动上晕倒一事都记忆犹新。

sentences.en: I think she had pneumonia.
sentences.zh: 我想她当时得了肺炎。

sentences.en: She had pneumonia.
sentences.zh: 她得了肺炎。

sentences.en: And, you know, the Clinton campaign, I think, is still quite resentful of the way that was covered.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，克林顿团队对当时的报道方式至今仍相当不满。

sentences.en: But a candidate collapsing in the middle of a general election is a relevant subject for coverage.
sentences.zh: 但候选人在大选中期虚脱晕倒是一个相关的报道话题。

sentences.en: President Trump's lack of transparency about his health has been a huge subject for coverage over the last few years.
sentences.zh: 过去几年里，特朗普总统对自己的健康状况缺乏透明度一直是各大媒体报道的重点。

sentences.en: There's enormous suspicion about whether we really know everything that we deserve to know about the president's health.
sentences.zh: 人们极度怀疑我们是否真正了解了所有关于总统健康、我们应当了解的情况。

sentences.en: So this is not bias against Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是针对伯尼·桑德斯的偏见。

sentences.en: But the fact that people are inclined to see it as bias against Bernie Sanders, again, underscores the strength of his support.
sentences.zh: 但人们倾向于将其视为对伯尼·桑德斯的偏见这一事实，再次凸显了他支持力量的强大。

sentences.en: So you mentioned Hillary Clinton in 2016.
sentences.zh: 所以你提到了2016年的希拉里·克林顿。

sentences.en: Jessica encountered a lot of supporters who very much wanted to go back to that race and talk about what happened the last time around.
sentences.zh: 杰西遇到了许多选民，他们非常希望回到那场竞选中，谈论上一次发生了什么。

sentences.en: And I want to play some of that.
sentences.zh: 我想播放其中的一些片段。

sentences.en: We need to get Bernie elected this time around.
sentences.zh: 我们这次需要选出伯尼。

sentences.en: The DNC screwed him over in 2016.
sentences.zh: 民主党全国委员会在2016年坑了他。

sentences.en: He was robbed of the nomination.
sentences.zh: 他的提名被剥夺了。

sentences.en: So people want Bernie.
sentences.zh: 所以人们想要伯尼。

sentences.en: I think it's the race we needed to have in 2016.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是我们在2016年本该有的竞选。

sentences.en: I think there's a populist field going on.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在有一种民粹主义的浪潮正在发生。

sentences.en: The elites are destroying the country and and the Democrats lost because we ran an elitiSt.
sentences.zh: 精英阶层正在毁灭国家，而民主党之所以输了，是因为我们推选了一个精英主义者。

sentences.en: And now it's time to run a candidate with a multiracial working class coalition.
sentences.zh: 现在是时候推出一位拥有多元种族工人阶级联盟的候选人了。

sentences.en: The Democrats are just as corrupt as Republicans because there's been evidence that the DNC did screw with caucuses, that in Seattle, he won by a landslide.
sentences.zh: 民主党和共和党一样腐败，因为有证据表明民主党全国委员会确实干预了党团会议，在西雅图，他是压倒性获胜。

sentences.en: But the delegates voted for Hillary anyway.
sentences.zh: 但党代表们最后还是把票投给了希拉里。

sentences.en: So, Alex, what do you make of that?
sentences.zh: 那么，亚历克斯，你对此怎么看？

sentences.en: I think there are a lot of myths about the role of the DNC in 2016.
sentences.zh: 我认为关于2016年民主党全国委员会角色的说法存在很多误区。

sentences.en: But the valid core to all of that is the sense among Sanders supporters, and this is really not up for debate,
sentences.zh: 但所有这一切的核心合理之处在于桑德斯支持者的一种普遍感受，而这其实是毋庸置疑的：

sentences.en: that the Democratic Party establishment did everything they could to give Hillary Clinton an advantage over him in that primary.
sentences.zh: 民主党建制派竭尽所能地为希拉里·克林顿在初选中对付他提供优势。

sentences.en: Remind us of that just so we can have it in hand.
sentences.zh: 提醒我们一下，好让我们心里有个数。

sentences.en: You had everyone at the top of the party, including President Obama, do what they could to clear the field for Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 党内最高层的所有人，包括奥巴马总统，都尽其所能为希拉里·克林顿清场。

sentences.en: You had the leadership of the party in both houses of Congress try to clear the way for Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 国会两院的党内领导层也试图为希拉里·克林顿扫清道路。

sentences.en: You had other kinds of coordination between party officials who were supposed to be neutral, who are ostensibly neutral,
sentences.zh: 你还会发现本应保持中立、表面上应该中立的党内官员之间，

sentences.en: and leaders of the Clinton campaign in ways that none of it was illegal and none of it was outside of the American political tradition.
sentences.zh: 与克林顿竞选团队的领导人之间存在其他形式的协调，尽管这些都不违法，也都没有脱离美国政治传统的范畴。

sentences.en: But if you're a Bernie Sanders supporter and you looked at that and you felt like there ought to be an even playing field in this race, there wasn't.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是伯尼·桑德斯的支持者，你看到这些就会觉得这场竞选本该有个公平的竞争环境，但并没有。

sentences.en: I wonder how that makes a Bernie Sanders supporter relate to the Democratic Party, especially if Sanders starts to falter.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这会让伯尼·桑德斯的支持者如何看待民主党，特别是如果桑德斯开始失利的话。

sentences.en: This is one of the Trumpiest things about Bernie Sanders and his political movement, that in 2015, 2016,
sentences.zh: 这是伯尼·桑德斯及其政治运动中最具特朗普风格的特征之一，即在2015年、2016年，

sentences.en: one of the best predictors of support for Donald Trump in the Republican primary was dislike for the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 共和党初选中预测对唐纳德·特朗普支持度的最佳指标之一，就是对共和党的厌恶。

sentences.en: He has obviously now come to embody the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 他现在显然已经成为了共和党的化身。

sentences.en: So that dynamic has changed.
sentences.zh: 所以这种动态已经改变了。

sentences.en: But you have a lot of people in the Democratic Party or on the left who are Democratic primary voters supporting Bernie Sanders and do not like the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 但民主党内或左翼阵营中有许多人是支持伯尼·桑德斯的民主党初选选民，同时又讨厌民主党。

sentences.en: Something that really frustrates a more mainline Democrats that they feel like Bernie is this interloper who is sort of rousing the left against the only party that really speaks to them.
sentences.zh: 这让一些主流民主党人感到非常沮丧，他们觉得伯尼是个闯入者，某种程度上是在煽动左翼去对抗唯一真正代表他们的政党。

sentences.en: But if you are a Bernie Sanders supporter, you look at the traditional Democratic Party establishment as a collection of people and ideas that have failed.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是伯尼·桑德斯的支持者，你会将传统的民主党建制派视为一帮已经失败的人和理念的集合体。

sentences.en: And what about the candidates?
sentences.zh: 那候选人们呢？

sentences.en: Well, that is one of the great questions of this race.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是这场竞选中最大的问题之一。

sentences.en: If Bernie is not the nominee, whether his core supporters will embrace another candidate with similar enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 如果伯尼未能获得提名，他的核心支持者是否会以同样的热情去支持另一位候选人。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 纽约时报App？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 免费解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能阅读所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《纽约时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》App时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看时报订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载时报App，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: One of the candidates, Elizabeth Warren, shares very similar policy positions.
sentences.zh: 其中一位候选人伊丽莎白·沃伦，有着非常相似的政策立场。

sentences.en: She's also a liberal populiSt.
sentences.zh: 她也是一位自由派民粹主义者。

sentences.en: I wonder what makes you continue your support for Bernie over Elizabeth Warren?
sentences.zh: 我很好奇是什么让你选择继续支持伯尼而不是伊丽莎白·沃伦？

sentences.en: Warren calls herself a capitalist and she's not out for a political revolution.
sentences.zh: 沃伦自称是资本主义者，她并不打算搞政治革命。

sentences.en: She is taking all of Bernie's policies and kind of putting a spin on it.
sentences.zh: 她拿了伯尼所有的政策，然后加入了自己的包装。

sentences.en: And it's like, do you have any original ideas?
sentences.zh: 这就好比，你有什么原创想法吗？

sentences.en: And if she believed in these things, why wasn't she supporting them four years ago?
sentences.zh: 如果她真的相信这些事情，为什么四年前她不支持呢？

sentences.en: I think Medicare for all is a big one.
sentences.zh: 我认为全民医保是一个重大议题。

sentences.en: I don't know if I trust Warren.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我是否信任沃伦。

sentences.en: She says she's for it, but it took her a long time to get there.
sentences.zh: 她说她支持，但她花了很长时间才走到这一步。

sentences.en: And, you know, Warren used to be a Republican.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，沃伦以前是个共和党人。

sentences.en: Warren used to be a Republican.
sentences.zh: 沃伦以前是个共和党人。

sentences.en: She was a Republican.
sentences.zh: 她曾经是共和党人。

sentences.en: And so, like, Elizabeth Warren, I feel like, is just a watered-down form of Bernie to try to make her more appealing.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得伊丽莎白·沃伦就像是伯尼的一个淡化版本，用来让她更具吸引力。

sentences.en: But the second the primary is over, she's just going to pivot.
sentences.zh: 但初选一结束，她就会立刻转变立场。

sentences.en: Well, look, that's really striking.
sentences.zh: 听着，这真的很让人震惊。

sentences.en: She's not been a Republican since I was in primary school, which was a while ago.
sentences.zh: 在我上小学的时候，她就已经不是共和党人了，那已经是挺久以前的事了。

sentences.en: But the fact that Sanders supporters have latched onto that in the way they have, I think,
sentences.zh: 但桑德斯支持者以这种方式揪住这一点不放，我认为，

sentences.en: reflects just the gap in trust between how they feel about Bernie and how they feel about almost literally any other politician,
sentences.zh: 这恰恰反映了他们对伯尼的感受与对几乎其他任何政治家的感受之间存在的信任鸿沟，

sentences.en: certainly any other politician running for president.
sentences.zh: 当然也包括任何其他竞选总统的政治家。

sentences.en: It still feels surprising to hear Sanders supporters attempt to differentiate a Democratic rival who, on paper, is so ideologically similar.
sentences.zh: 听到桑德斯的支持者试图与一位在纸面上意识形态如此相似的民主党竞争对手划清界限，依然让人感到意外。

sentences.en: I think there are some important ideological distinctions, at least in the abstract, that I think in Elizabeth Warren's ideal world, we would be a heavily regulated,
sentences.zh: 我认为在意识形态上存在一些重要的区别，至少在抽象意义上是这样，我认为在伊丽莎白·沃伦的理想世界里，我们会是一个高度监管、

sentences.en: heavily enforced free market economy, that it would be something similar to FDR, Teddy Roosevelt kind of regulatory regime.
sentences.zh: 高度强制的自由市场经济，那将类似于罗斯福、西奥多·罗斯福那样的监管体制。

sentences.en: Bernie Sanders would, I think, in his ideal world have us much closer to a sort of Scandinavian social democracy,
sentences.zh: 而我认为，伯尼·桑德斯的理想世界会让我们更接近某种斯堪的纳维亚式的社会民主主义，

sentences.en: which is a really fundamentally different way of approaching government.
sentences.zh: 这是一种本质上截然不同的处理政府事务的方式。

sentences.en: And part of this is a dynamic that happens in primaries generally,
sentences.zh: 部分原因是在初选中普遍存在的一种动态，

sentences.en: that the candidates who are ideologically closest together can end up having the most sort of intense hostility between their supporters because they feel like only one of these people can emerge from this.
sentences.zh: 意识形态最接近的候选人，其支持者之间最终可能会产生最激烈的敌意，因为他们觉得这些人中只能有一个胜出。

sentences.en: And they're right, but there is, I think, also a level of seeing the trees but not the forest here,
sentences.zh: 他们是对的，但我认为这也存在一种只见树木、不见森林的心理，

sentences.en: where you have the number two and number three candidates in this Democratic primary, if they were nominated,
sentences.zh: 民主党初选中的第二和第三名候选人，如果他们获得提名，

sentences.en: would be the most liberal nominee in certainly my lifetime and in lifetimes a good deal longer than mine as well.
sentences.zh: 那绝对是我有生之年里最自由派的候选人，甚至在我有生之年更长的岁月里也是如此。

sentences.en: So the level of frustration does seem sort of out of proportion to what the downside of an Elizabeth Warren nomination would be.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种挫败感似乎与伊丽莎白·沃伦获得提名所带来的负面影响完全不成比例。

sentences.en: So, Alex, to your point about the forest for the trees, Jess asked a lot of these voters, if Sanders doesn't win,
sentences.zh: 所以，亚历克斯，针对你刚才关于只见树木不见森林的观点，杰斯问了许多这样的选民：如果桑德斯没有赢，

sentences.en: are you fine voting for anybody else in the party who becomes the nominee?
sentences.zh: 你还能接受党内其他任何获得提名的候选人吗？

sentences.en: And this is what people said.
sentences.zh: 这就是大家的回答。

sentences.en: And who is your second candidate of choice?
sentences.zh: 你心目中的第二候选人是谁？

sentences.en: Elizabeth Warren.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·沃伦。

sentences.en: If Bernie can't make it, I'm happy with Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 如果伯尼不能胜出，我对伊丽莎白也很满意。

sentences.en: If either Elizabeth Warren or Bernie Sanders win the nomination, I would be so happy.
sentences.zh: 如果伊丽莎白·沃伦或伯尼·桑德斯赢得提名，我会非常高兴。

sentences.en: And I think it would be, again, a sign of how much the Democratic Party is shifting.
sentences.zh: 我认为这再次表明了民主党正在发生多么巨大的转变。

sentences.en: I do like Elizabeth Warren's policies.
sentences.zh: 我确实喜欢伊丽莎白·沃伦的政策。

sentences.en: And, like, if Elizabeth Warren is the nominee, I'll, like, happily vote for her.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果伊丽莎白·沃伦获得提名，我会很乐意投票给她。

sentences.en: So a lot of them, despite their skepticism of Warren, say, if I had to, I would vote for Elizabeth Warren.
sentences.zh: 所以他们中的许多人，尽管对沃伦持怀疑态度，但还是表示：如果必须的话，我会投票给伊丽莎白·沃伦。

sentences.en: But then there were several voters who said that they would be very hard-pressed to turn out for anyone who wasn't Bernie or what they consider to be kind of Bernie-lite,
sentences.zh: 但也有几位选民表示，要让他们去支持任何不是伯尼、或者不是他们眼中所谓的“伯尼轻量版”（也就是沃伦）的人，会非常勉强，

sentences.en: which is Warren.
sentences.zh: 也就是沃伦。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So I like Liz Warren.
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢莉兹·沃伦。

sentences.en: I think she's probably the only other candidate I would ever even consider supporting.
sentences.zh: 我想她可能是除伯尼外我唯一会考虑支持的候选人。

sentences.en: The rest of them I find to be rather embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 其余的人我都觉得相当拿不出手。

sentences.en: If it wasn't Bernie, who's your second candidate of choice?
sentences.zh: 如果不是伯尼，你心目中的第二候选人是谁？

sentences.en: If it wasn't, I would probably vote for Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 如果不是他，我可能会投票给伊丽莎白。

sentences.en: If she was the candidate, I wouldn't vote for Biden.
sentences.zh: 如果她是候选人，我就不会投票给拜登。

sentences.en: That's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有意思。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I guess, as they say in the Senate, I should revise and extend what I said about people sort of missing the forest,
sentences.zh: 我想，正如他们在参议院所说的那样，我应该修正并补充我之前关于人们有点忽略大局的说法，

sentences.en: that you do hear people there sort of recognizing that the party as a whole has moved, that there are candidates besides Bernie,
sentences.zh: 你会听到那里的人们某种程度上认识到整个党已经发生了变化，除了伯尼还有其他候选人，

sentences.en: although clearly anyone else would be the second best choice in this race for them.
sentences.zh: 尽管对他们来说，显然其他人在这场竞选中只能是第二选择。

sentences.en: But I think what you heard is how hard it will be for a candidate who is not an economic populist to speak to this set of voters,
sentences.zh: 但我认为你听到的是，对于一个不是经济民粹主义者的候选人来说，要想跟这批选民对话会有多难，

sentences.en: that if you end up with a candidate who is an avowed centrist or a nominee who has repudiated what Bernie Sanders stands for, hasn't just revised or watered down his views,
sentences.zh: 如果你最后选出了一位公开的温和派候选人，或者一个公开否认伯尼·桑德斯主张的提名人，他不仅仅是修正或淡化了伯尼的观点，

sentences.en: but has rejected them and attacked them, that's going to be a real challenge in the general election.
sentences.zh: 而是直接拒绝甚至攻击这些观点，那在大选中将是一个真正的挑战。

sentences.en: I think one of the calculations that Democrats have traditionally made, certainly made in 2016, is that the left will come home at the end of the day.
sentences.zh: 我认为民主党人传统上做出的盘算之一，在2016年肯定也做过，那就是左翼最终还是会归队。

sentences.en: And I think you saw in 2016 that was a risky bet to make.
sentences.zh: 我认为你在2016年看到，那是一个风险很大的赌注。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, that was a bet that just did not come true because when Sanders supporters were asked to support Hillary Clinton, many of them did not.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是一个并未兑现的赌注，因为当桑德斯的支持者被要求支持希拉里·克林顿的时候，许多人并没有这样做。

sentences.en: In fact, as we know from Times analysis, a meaningful number of them voted for Trump.
sentences.zh: 事实上，正如我们从《时报》的分析中得知的，其中相当一部分人把票投给了特朗普。

sentences.en: In the 2016 primary, it wasn't just liberals who voted for Sanders in the Democratic primary.
sentences.zh: 在2016年的初选中，在民主党初选中投票给桑德斯的不只有自由派。

sentences.en: There were people who were just sort of disaffected and outside the system, people who wanted a populist,
sentences.zh: 还有那些心怀不满、游离于体制之外的人，那些想要民粹主义者的人，

sentences.en: not necessarily somebody who is an ideological liberal as we traditionally think of it, people who just didn't like Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 不一定是我们传统意义上认为的意识形态上的自由派，而只是不喜欢希拉里·克林顿的人。

sentences.en: And then in the general election, there were people who were Democrats who just weren't enthusiastic.
sentences.zh: 然后在大选中，有一些民主党人只是缺乏热情。

sentences.en: They would have turned out to vote for Bernie Sanders, would have volunteered for Bernie Sanders, would have donated to Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 他们本会出来为伯尼·桑德斯投票，本会为伯尼·桑德斯当志愿者，本会向伯尼·桑德斯捐款。

sentences.en: And when you start to look at the margins of defeat for Hillary Clinton in the states that made the difference, Wisconsin, Michigan, Pennsylvania,
sentences.zh: 当你开始审视希拉里·克林顿在那些决定胜负的关键州（威斯康星州、密歇根州、宾夕法尼亚州）落败的微弱票差时，

sentences.en: could Democratic enthusiasm have turned out an additional 70,000 voters?
sentences.zh: 民主党人的热情本能多争取到7万名选民吗？

sentences.en: Very possibly.
sentences.zh: 很有可能。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So not to be too prescriptive, but based on everything you're saying, if Joe Biden is the nominee, it will be a challenge,
sentences.zh: 所以，不是说要指手画脚，但根据你所说的一切，如果乔·拜登获得提名，这将是一个挑战，

sentences.en: maybe a significant challenge for this group of voters to be won over and transferred to him.
sentences.zh: 对这群选民来说，要赢得他们的支持并把选票转移给他，或许是个不小的挑战。

sentences.en: If it is Elizabeth Warren, that will be more logical, although it will not necessarily be seamless.
sentences.zh: 如果是伊丽莎白·沃伦，情况会更符合逻辑，尽管未必会天衣无缝。

sentences.en: I think that's probably a safe bet.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很可能是十拿九稳的。

sentences.en: And if you're Joe Biden, you know, maybe you can bring these people around.
sentences.zh: 如果你是乔·拜登，你知道的，也许你能把这些人争取过来。

sentences.en: Maybe you need to make up for a lack of enthusiasm on the left by winning over voters closer to the political middle, even folks on the center right.
sentences.zh: 也许你需要通过争取政治中间派、甚至中右翼的选民，来弥补左翼热情的不足。

sentences.en: That's clearly a bet that candidates like Joe Biden are making, that if Bernie has his populist following, that would be much more enthusiastic about him than about me.
sentences.zh: 这显然是像乔·拜登这样的候选人正在下的赌注：如果伯尼有他的民粹主义追随者，他们对伯尼的热情会远超对我。

sentences.en: Well, I have moderates who will never vote for a Democratic socialist, but who I can turn out in a general election.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我这里有永远不会投票给民主党社会主义者、但我能在总选中动员起来的温和派。

sentences.en: And in a lot of ways, this is the big strategic debate in the Democratic Party right now.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，这就是目前民主党内部重大的战略辩论。

sentences.en: We've talked a lot about the ideological and policy debates in the party.
sentences.zh: 我们已经讨论了很多党内的意识形态和政策辩论。

sentences.en: But sort of fundamental to the Democratic race right now is,
sentences.zh: 但目前民主党竞选的核心在于：

sentences.en: are you better off trying to marshal a really enthusiastic and diverse coalition on the left or a more ideologically diverse coalition that is somewhat less reliant on liberal enthusiasm?
sentences.zh: 你是最好尝试在左翼凝聚一个非常热情且多元的联盟，还是一个意识形态更多元、在某种程度上不那么依赖自由派热情的联盟？

sentences.en: For whoever the nominee is in this election, and I think probably in most elections going forward,
sentences.zh: 无论谁是这次大选的提名人，而且我认为可能在未来的大多数选举中，

sentences.en: just given the ideological and demographic trajectory of the Democratic Party and the country, it's going to be a recurring challenge for them.
sentences.zh: 鉴于民主党和国家意识形态与人口结构的发展轨迹，这将是他们面临的一个反复出现的挑战。

sentences.en: How do you harness what Bernie Sanders has created, while also appealing broadly to the voters that you need in order to capture the nomination,
sentences.zh: 你如何在利用伯尼·桑德斯所创建的政治资产的同时，广泛吸引赢得提名所需的选民，

sentences.en: because Sanders is not actually doing that right now, and win a general election, which Sanders has never had the chance to try to do?
sentences.zh: 因为桑德斯目前实际上并没有做到这一点，并且赢得桑德斯从未有机会尝试去赢取的大选？

sentences.en: It's a particularly important question when you look to the future of the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 当你展望民主党未来时，这是一个尤为重要的问题。

sentences.en: If you were to sort of make a bet right now about the trajectory of that party over the next few years,
sentences.zh: 如果你现在要对该党未来几年的发展轨迹下一个赌注，

sentences.en: it will probably look more and more like the Bernie Sanders base and less and less like the coalition that defeated him in 2016 if the party stays on its current course.
sentences.zh: 如果该党保持目前的发展方向，它可能会越来越像伯尼·桑德斯的基层盘，而越来越不像2016年击败他的那个联盟。

sentences.en: This is a group of voters that is very much here to stay, and the question is, do they stay as engaged and enthusiastic Democrats?
sentences.zh: 这是一群短时间内不会消失的选民，问题是，他们会一直作为积极且热情的民主党人留下来吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Or do they basically start and finish their political journey with Bernie Sanders in a way that doesn't really help the party?
sentences.zh: 还是说他们基本上与伯尼·桑德斯一起开始并结束他们的政治征程，而这并不能真正帮助到党派？

sentences.en: Do they become passionate, lifelong Democratic voters, volunteers, donors,
sentences.zh: 他们会成为充满激情、终身的民主党选民、志愿者、捐赠者吗？

sentences.en: or do they go back to being either casually engaged with politics or disengaged entirely or really sort of disgusted with the party as they were in 2016?
sentences.zh: 还是说他们又恢复到对政治漫不经心、完全不关心，或者像2016年那样对这个党感到十分厌恶的状态？

sentences.en: Alex, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: OK, I have introduced a resolution today with Senator McConnell,
sentences.zh: 好的，我今天与参议员麦康奈尔共同提出了一项决议，

sentences.en: and the purpose of the resolution is to let the House know that the process you're engaging in regarding the attempted impeachment of President Trump is a substantial deviation from what the House has done in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 这项决议的目的是让众议院知道，你们目前针对弹劾特朗普总统所进行的程序，与众议院以往的做法有着本质上的偏离。

sentences.en: The Republican campaign to challenge the legitimacy of the House impeachment inquiry escalated on Thursday as Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina introduced a resolution condemning it as unorthodox and improper.
sentences.zh: 周四，随着南卡罗来纳州参议员林赛·格雷厄姆提出一项谴责众议院弹劾调查非正统且不正当的决议，共和党人挑战该调查合法性的行动再度升级。

sentences.en: However, Graham focused on the closed-door hearings led by Representative Adam Schiff,
sentences.zh: 然而，格雷厄姆将矛头指向了由众议员亚当·希夫主导的闭门听证会，

sentences.en: despite the fact that Republicans themselves conducted closed-door testimony during the impeachment of President Clinton in 1998.
sentences.zh: 尽管在1998年对克林顿总统的弹劾期间，共和党人自己也进行过闭门作证。

sentences.en: And in his latest effort to break the deadlock over Brexit, after yet another major delay, Prime Minister Boris Johnson said he would seek a new general election in December.
sentences.zh: 在又一次重大延期之后，首相鲍里斯·约翰逊为打破脱欧僵局做出了最新努力，他表示将寻求在12月份举行新的大选。

sentences.en: We're being very, very reasonable.
sentences.zh: 我们一直表现得非常非常通情达理。

sentences.en: We're saying, if you genuinely want more time, you can have it.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是，如果你真的想要更多时间，你可以拥有。

sentences.en: Here it is.
sentences.zh: 时间就在这里。

sentences.en: But the condition for that is that we all agree to go for a general election on December the 12th.
sentences.zh: 但前提是大家都同意在12月12日举行大选。

sentences.en: Johnson hopes that such an election would give him a popular mandate to carry out his vision of a swift Brexit, despite deep resistance within Parliament,
sentences.zh: 约翰逊希望这样一场大选能赋予他民意授权，以实现他迅速脱欧的设想，尽管议会内部存在强烈的阻力，

sentences.en: whose support is needed for such an election.
sentences.zh: 而举行这样的大选需要议会的支持。

sentences.en: In an interview with the BBC, Johnson defended the strategy,
sentences.zh: 在接受BBC采访时，约翰逊为这一策略进行了辩护，

sentences.en: which his opponents in Parliament say is a form of political intimidation designed to scare them into supporting his plan.
sentences.zh: 议会中的反对派则称这是一种政治恐吓，旨在吓唬他们支持其计划。

sentences.en: But, Prime Minister, it's not standard behaviour.
sentences.zh: 但是，首相先生，这并非标准做法。

sentences.en: You're essentially trying to blackmail Parliament with the threat of an election in order to ram through your bill.
sentences.zh: 你本质上是在用大选的威胁来勒海议会，以便强行通过你的法案。

sentences.en: You could just say, fine, let's have as long as it takes to get through this line by line in Parliament.
sentences.zh: 你大可以直说，好吧，让我们花尽可能长的时间在议会里逐字逐句地通过它。

sentences.en: Would that not be the responsible thing to do?
sentences.zh: 难道这不才是负责任的做法吗？

sentences.en: No, come on.
sentences.zh: 不，拜托。

sentences.en: We've had three and a half years of this.
sentences.zh: 我们已经为此折腾了三年半。

sentences.en: Not looking at this bill.
sentences.zh: 而不是在看这个法案。

sentences.zh: 本期《每日新闻》由西奥·巴尔科姆制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯伯格创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Sam Dolnik, Michaela Bouchard, Stella Tam, Lauren Jackson, and Julia Simon.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢萨姆·多尔尼克、米凯拉·布沙尔、斯特拉·谭、劳伦·杰克逊和朱莉娅·西蒙。
zh_words: 米凯拉·布沙尔、斯特拉·谭

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》就是这样。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Bavaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴瓦罗。

sentences.en: See you on Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场残酷、混乱且有时令人兴奋的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我莎拉·科尼格主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，讲述了人们试图维持其影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
